lecture.New_Day8Part1audio01.mp3: Welcome to Day 8! Today, we master temporal data analysis with Date and Time functions. Managing timestamps accurately is a critical skill for computing business metrics like sales velocity, user churn, fulfillment SLA, and customer lifetime value.
lecture.New_Day8Part1audio02.mp3: In relational databases, dates follow the ISO-8601 standard: YYYY-MM-DD for dates, and YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS for timestamps. SQLite stores dates as TEXT, REAL, or INTEGER, and provides built-in date functions to parse and manipulate them reliably.
lecture.New_Day8Part1audio03.mp3: To retrieve the current timestamp, SQLite provides date of now for the current calendar date, time of now for clock time, and datetime of now for the full timestamp.
lecture.New_Day8Part1audio04.mp3: In Query 1, we inspect today's date and time. In Query 2, we compute elapsed days since an order was placed by subtracting the Julian day of the order date from the Julian day of now.
lecture.New_Day8Part1audio05.mp3: Calculating intervals between two dates is essential for fulfillment SLAs. In SQLite, the julianday function converts dates into floating-point day numbers. Subtracting two Julian days yields the exact elapsed days between them.
lecture.New_Day8Part1audio06.mp3: In Query 1, we calculate fulfillment duration in days between order date and shipped date, casting the result to an integer. In Query 2, we calculate employee tenure in days from their hire date.
lecture.New_Day8Part1audio07.mp3: Date arithmetic lets you project forward or look backwards in time. The date function accepts modifier strings such as plus 30 days, minus 3 months, or plus 1 year.
lecture.New_Day8Part1audio08.mp3: In Query 1, we compute delivery deadlines by adding 30 days to order dates. In Query 2, we filter for recent orders by comparing order dates against date of now with minus 90 days.
lecture.New_Day8Part1audio09.mp3: The strftime function is SQLite's Swiss Army knife for formatting and extracting temporal components. It takes a format string and a date column.
lecture.New_Day8Part1audio10.mp3: Key format codes include: percent Y for 4-digit year, percent m for 2-digit month, percent d for 2-digit day of month, and percent w for day of week where zero represents Sunday.
lecture.New_Day8Part1audio11.mp3: In the demonstration query, we extract order year, order month, and order day as distinct columns, enabling temporal group-by rollups.
lecture.New_Day8Part1audio12.mp3: Aggregating by date parts is standard practice in financial reporting. By grouping orders by strftime of percent Y, we calculate annual order volume and total revenue per calendar year.
lecture.New_Day8Part1audio13.mp3: To group by year and month together, format the date as percent Y dash percent m. This creates chronological monthly cohorts for trend analysis.
lecture.New_Day8Part1audio14.mp3: Watch out for sargability when filtering dates: avoid wrapping columns inside functions in the WHERE clause when an indexed date column exists. Writing order date greater than or equal to 2026-01-01 allows index scans, unlike wrapping the column in strftime.
lecture.New_Day8Part1audio15.mp3: Cross-database comparison: MySQL uses DATE_ADD, DATE_SUB, and DATEDIFF. PostgreSQL uses date math operators and the EXTRACT function. SQLite uses date, datetime, julianday, and strftime.
lecture.New_Day8Part1audio16.mp3: You're now ready to tackle real-world date and time challenges. Let's enter the practice arena and solve business problems involving tenure, fulfillment lag, and monthly revenue trends!

questions.New_Day8Question01.mp3: Retrieve today's date! Write a query to return the current system date as today using the date function.
questions.New_Day8Question01sol.mp3: Let's retrieve today's date. SELECT date of now as today.
questions.New_Day8Question02.mp3: Extract the order year! From the orders table, return order ID, order date, and the four-digit year extracted using strftime as order year.
questions.New_Day8Question02sol.mp3: Let's extract the 4-digit year. SELECT order ID, order date, strftime of percent Y comma order date as order year... FROM orders.
questions.New_Day8Question03.mp3: Filter orders by calendar year! Return order ID, customer ID, order date, and total amount for all orders placed in the year 2024 using strftime.
questions.New_Day8Question03sol.mp3: Let's filter for 2024 orders. SELECT order ID, customer ID, order date, total amount... FROM orders... WHERE strftime of percent Y comma order date equals 2024.
questions.New_Day8Question04.mp3: Project delivery deadlines! For all orders, return order ID, order date, and a projected delivery deadline calculated by adding 7 days to order date as deadline.
questions.New_Day8Question04sol.mp3: Let's project 7 days forward. SELECT order ID, order date, date of order date comma plus 7 days as deadline... FROM orders.
questions.New_Day8Question05.mp3: Calculate employee tenure in days! From employees, return employee ID, first name, hire date, and tenure in days calculated using julianday from hire date to now, cast as an integer.
questions.New_Day8Question05sol.mp3: Let's compute employee tenure. SELECT employee ID, first name, hire date, CAST of julianday of now minus julianday of hire date as INTEGER as tenure days... FROM employees.
questions.New_Day8Question06.mp3: Measure shipping fulfillment latency! From orders, return order ID, order date, shipped date, and the fulfillment lag in days between order date and shipped date for all orders where shipped date is not null.
questions.New_Day8Question06sol.mp3: Let's measure shipping days. SELECT order ID, order date, shipped date, CAST of julianday of shipped date minus julianday of order date as INTEGER as fulfillment days... FROM orders... WHERE shipped date IS NOT NULL.
questions.New_Day8Question07.mp3: Monthly revenue rollup! Group orders by year and month formatted as YYYY-MM using strftime as order month, returning order month, total orders, and total revenue.
questions.New_Day8Question07sol.mp3: Let's aggregate by month. SELECT strftime of percent Y dash percent m comma order date as order month, count star as total orders, SUM of total amount as total revenue... FROM orders... GROUP BY order month... ORDER BY order month.
questions.New_Day8Question08.mp3: Identify weekend shopping trends! Filter orders for purchases placed on a weekend, where strftime percent w equals 0 for Sunday or 6 for Saturday. Return order ID, order date, and total amount.
questions.New_Day8Question08sol.mp3: Let's filter for weekend orders. SELECT order ID, order date, total amount... FROM orders... WHERE strftime of percent w comma order date IN 0 comma 6.
questions.New_Day8Question09.mp3: Annual orders summary! Group orders by year extracted using strftime, showing order year and the total number of orders placed in each year, sorted chronologically.
questions.New_Day8Question09sol.mp3: Let's count orders per year. SELECT strftime of percent Y comma order date as order year, count star as total orders... FROM orders... GROUP BY order year... ORDER BY order year.
questions.New_Day8Question10.mp3: Find senior staff with over 700 days of tenure! From employees, return first name, hire date, and tenure days where tenure exceeds 700 days, ordered from most senior to least.
questions.New_Day8Question10sol.mp3: Let's filter by tenure. SELECT first name, hire date, CAST of julianday of now minus julianday of hire date as INTEGER as tenure days... FROM employees... WHERE julianday of now minus julianday of hire date is greater than 700... ORDER BY tenure days DESC.
questions.New_Day8Question11.mp3: Audit slow fulfillment! Find orders where shipping took more than 3 days. Return order ID, customer ID, order date, and fulfillment days, sorted with the slowest first.
questions.New_Day8Question11sol.mp3: Let's filter slow orders. SELECT order ID, customer ID, order date, CAST of julianday of shipped date minus julianday of order date as INTEGER as fulfillment days... FROM orders... WHERE shipped date IS NOT NULL AND julianday of shipped date minus julianday of order date is greater than 3... ORDER BY fulfillment days DESC.
questions.New_Day8Question12.mp3: Extract day of the week metrics! Group orders by day of the week number using strftime percent w as day of week, returning day of week, total orders, and average total amount rounded to 2 decimals.
questions.New_Day8Question12sol.mp3: Let's group by day of the week. SELECT strftime of percent w comma order date as day of week, count star as total orders, ROUND of average function of total amount comma 2 as avg order val... FROM orders... GROUP BY day of week... ORDER BY day of week.
questions.New_Day8Question13.mp3: Calculate 30-day payment return deadlines! For completed orders, return order ID, total amount, and date of order date plus 30 days as return deadline.
questions.New_Day8Question13sol.mp3: Let's project return deadlines. SELECT order ID, total amount, date of order date comma plus 30 days as return deadline... FROM orders... WHERE status equals Completed.
questions.New_Day8Question14.mp3: Quarterly sales reporting! Group orders by year and quarter using strftime to format year and compute the quarter, returning order year, total revenue, and order count.
questions.New_Day8Question14sol.mp3: Let's aggregate by year and status. SELECT strftime of percent Y comma order date as order year, status, count star as order count, SUM of total amount as total revenue... FROM orders... GROUP BY order year, status... ORDER BY order year, status.
questions.New_Day8Question15.mp3: Comprehensive temporal audit! Return customer ID, count of orders, earliest order date as first order, and latest order date as last order from orders, for customers with more than 1 order.
questions.New_Day8Question15sol.mp3: Let's analyze customer order lifespan. SELECT customer ID, count star as order count, MIN of order date as first order, MAX of order date as last order... FROM orders... GROUP BY customer ID... HAVING count star is greater than 1... ORDER BY order count DESC.
